title: Deriving Semantic Checkers from Tests to Detect Silent Failures in Production Distributed Systems
problem: Silent failures in distributed systems (partial failures, state inconsistencies) aren't caught by standard testing, causing production outages
motivation: Reliable distributed systems are critical for AI infrastructure; automated detection of silent failures improves system trustworthiness
method: The approach automatically extracts rules about correct system behavior from existing test cases and packages them as semantic checkers (tools that validate whether the system is behaving correctly). These checkers are deployed to production where they run continuously, comparing the actual system behavior to the expected behavior defined in the tests. When the system violates these rules, the checker flags a failure—including silent failures that don't crash the system or show obvious errors. By reusing tests this way, the system gains production monitoring without needing to manually write separate validation rules.
key_novelty: Automatically extracting semantic checkers from test cases to detect silent failures in production.
contributions: Automated semantic checker generation from tests
Detection of silent failures in production
limitations: Title-only paper; automation quality and coverage not specified; false positive/negative rates unknown
